newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen slightly weak, peso pressured.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen slightly weak, peso pressured.

text.p: --Mexico stocks viewed slightly weak on profit-taking
--Peso likely pressured from higher U.S. interest rates
--Cetes overnight rate seen volatile on election jitters
Traders said Mexican stocks were likely to open stable or slightly weak on Thursday, continuing at similar trading levels this week.
"(The IPC index) will continue with a weak downside tendency. People are getting used to the new prices," one desk trader said.
Technical analysts saw support at 4,400 points on the IPC scale, or 4,380 points in the short-term.
Traders expected the peso to be pressured because of higher U.S. interest rates on the 30-year treasury bonds.
Dealers predicted a range from 7.9550/7.9750 pesos per dollar for the 48-hour benchmark. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9565/7.9700 per dollar, compared to Wednesday's close of 7.9480/7.9570.
Higher U.S rates also were expected to provoke nervousness in overnight Cetes rates, seen moving up to around 21.50 percent because of end of the month liquidity pressures.
Jitters over the coming elections were said to be contributing to rate volatility..
Overnight rates on bank paper closed up 70 basis points on Wednesday at 21.25 percent amid the monthly demand for cash.
The U.S. 30-year treasury bond opened unchanged on Thursday.

A general dearth of news for the week was expected to stave off strong shifts in the market. Dealers said they were bracing for events next week and the July 6 election in Mexico of the Mexico City mayor and of key governors and deputies.
